outcome_intro: Running SaaS Alerts across a book of customers? Ask your AI "what fired overnight, critical first," "which Respond triggers expire next," or "is one IP hitting several clients" and get one answer instead of paging customer by customer. One partner key reaches all four SaaS Alerts APIs, including Respond, and contain and rule-triggers decide preview every change until you confirm it.

instead_of_say.say: What fired across all my customers since yesterday, critical first, grouped by customer and user?

instead_of_say.instead: Watching the Respond queue so manual-approval triggers are decided before they lapse (they auto-expire after 12 hours or when the rule fires again)
instead_of_say.say: Which Respond triggers expire in the next two hours, and what would approving each one do?

pain_points: Respond's manual-approval queue is on a clock. The Respond API documents that a manual approval "will auto expire when the rule triggers again or 12 hours whichever is earlier", and the SaaS Alerts help center ("Analyzing a Respond trigger") says a failed remediation is reminded every 15 minutes and automatically ignored after the third reminder. Working that queue across many customers means knowing which decision lapses first.

The Respond API needs a second credential, and its error hides that. In the r/msp thread "Kaseya Saas Alerts API" an MSP on the EU instance got "Only secure origins are allowed" on every call, and another replied they had been "banging my head against this same issue for weeks", suspecting CORS, with support tickets unanswered. The fix the thread landed on: POST to the auth endpoint first, then send the access token on every Respond call.

The noise is real. MSP reviewers of SaaS Alerts on G2 describe a flood of notifications until the configuration is tuned and false positives you learn to filter out over time, and Kaseya's own Tech Jam webinar spends a session on noise reduction. Tuning well means seeing which alerts repeat across customers, not one tenant at a time.

different_vs_wrappers: [WYRE-AI's saas-alerts-mcp](https://github.com/WYRE-AI/saas-alerts-mcp), which also backs the SaaS Alerts plugin in their msp-claude-plugins marketplace, exposes the SaaS Alerts External Partner API as 30 tools across customers, events, users, devices, billing, scheduled reports and partner settings, with no Respond, suppression or webhook tools. This connector covers all four SaaS Alerts APIs with one partner key, including Respond (it mints the Respond access token itself) and Webhooks, and syncs events into a local store so triage, cross-customer correlation and coverage gaps are one local query across every customer.
different_vs_vendor: It complements the SaaS Alerts dashboard rather than replacing it: the dashboard stays the place to configure monitoring, review alerts and set up Respond, while this skill brings cross-customer triage, the Respond queue by deadline, one-account investigations and coverage gaps to whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, and saas-alerts-mcp speaks HTTP natively: run `saas-alerts-mcp --transport http` with SAAS_ALERTS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN set (it serves `http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp` and requires that token as a bearer header) and put it behind an HTTPS gateway that ChatGPT can sign in to with OAuth and that adds that bearer header, since ChatGPT connectors do not send a fixed one. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my SaaS Alerts data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, the MCP server and the local store are all local, and the only network calls go to SaaS Alerts and to destinations you name. The local store holds your customers' account emails, sign-in IPs and event details, so treat your data directory like any other copy of that data. Each webhook subscription's delivery token is withheld before it is printed, cached or stored, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.

faqs.q: Where do I get the SaaS Alerts API key?
faqs.a: In the SaaS Alerts dashboard, open Settings > API and click GET APIKEY. SaaS Alerts shows the key only until you leave that page, so copy it then. Set it as SAAS_ALERTS_API_KEY. That one partner key reaches the Reports, Manage and Webhooks APIs, and the CLI exchanges it for the Respond access token on first use, so there is no second credential to paste. If every call answers 401 Access denied, ask SaaS Alerts support to enable the REST API for your account.

faqs.q: Why does the Respond API answer "Only secure origins are allowed"?
faqs.a: That is what Respond returns when a call carries the api_key but no access token. Respond needs a short-lived token minted from the partner key with POST /respondApi/api/v1/auth. This connector mints it on the first Respond call, sends it on every Respond request, keeps it in memory for that process only, and mints a fresh one once if Respond rejects it.

faqs.q: Can the AI block a user or approve Respond actions by itself?
faqs.a: Only if you let it. contain, rule-triggers decide and subscriptions health --reenable preview by default and change nothing until you add --confirm. The generated commands (rule-triggers approve, response-actions execute, customers delete and the rest) send as soon as they run, so preview them with --dry-run, which sends nothing. Over MCP, set SAAS_ALERTS_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 for an agent that should only read: saas-alerts_execute then runs GET endpoints only and the three workflow writers refuse --confirm.

Yes. The Respond API documents that a manual approval expires after 12 hours or when the rule triggers again, whichever is earlier, and the SaaS Alerts help center says a failed remediation is automatically ignored after the third 15-minute reminder. rule-triggers queue lists pending and failed triggers by that deadline, with the actions an approval would fire, and rule-triggers decide skips expired or superseded triggers unless you pass --include-expired. The API does not say whether "triggers again" means anywhere or for the same customer, so the CLI counts a trigger as superseded only by a newer one of the same rule for the same organization and accounts: it may show a trigger Respond already expired (Respond then refuses the approve), but it never hides a live one.

faqs.q: Why does triage say synced: false?
faqs.a: triage, investigate, cross-tenant and coverage read the local store, so they need a sync first, for example `saas-alerts-cli sync --resources customers,events --since 7d`. They say synced: false, with a note naming the fix, when the data they need was never synced, when the last events sync did not finish (an automatic refresh fetches one page at a time), or when the window you asked about starts before the oldest events you synced. An events sync narrowed with --param stores its rows but does not count as complete. An empty or partial result is never presented as an all-clear, and --select always keeps the synced and note fields.

faqs.q: Does contain work for Google Workspace accounts?
faqs.a: No. Respond response actions run against Microsoft 365 only, so contain refuses a Google Workspace or other non-Microsoft account, and stops when an email matches more than one Microsoft 365 account. The API returns no job id for an action, so contain reports each job match as best-effort and always says verified: false; check the account in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

faqs.q: Has it been tested against a live SaaS Alerts tenant?
faqs.a: Not yet. Every endpoint traces to SaaS Alerts' published API specs and the Respond token exchange was checked against the live API without a key, but no partner has run it against real data yet. Two things wait on a live tenant: a partially rejected sync is reported as a sync_warning, so sync --strict can still exit 0 when some pages were refused; and the Unify device lists page with searchAfter from the response's meta.sort as the Manage spec describes, but if a tenant returns a bare list instead, a partner with more than 1,000 devices cannot sync them completely (sync and devices list --all then say truncated, never complete). Run it, and tell us what you find.

faqs.q: Does it replace the SaaS Alerts dashboard?
faqs.a: No. The dashboard stays best for configuring monitoring, reviewing individual alerts and setting up Respond. This skill answers the across-every-customer questions and runs reviewed actions from your AI agent.

governance_summary: The skill authenticates with your SaaS Alerts partner API key, and that one key reaches every customer and all four APIs; SaaS Alerts documents no read-only or per-customer key. Triage, investigate, cross-tenant, coverage, the Respond queue and every list, get or report are read-only and safe to let an agent run. Approving Respond triggers, contain and response actions lock real Microsoft 365 users out, and whitelists, suppressions and Respond rules change what gets detected, so those need a human to approve the exact command. Generated commands run immediately, so set SAAS_ALERTS_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 for an agent that should only read.
